title: Kalshi ditches Trump Jr. as advisor; CEO admitted "optics" weren't good
gist: Kalshi ended Donald Trump Jr.'s advisory role after his firm 1789 Capital invested $300 million in rival Polymarket, though he may retain a Kalshi equity stake. The piece details how the Trump administration's CFTC is backing prediction markets against state gambling regulators, while Kalshi keeps losing state cases and faces a possible Supreme Court fight with New Jersey.

insights.claim: Kalshi and Donald Trump Jr. mutually ended his advisory role after his venture firm 1789 Capital made a $300 million investment in rival Polymarket, reported in August 2026, building on a smaller August 2025 investment; Trump Jr. is also a Polymarket advisor.
insights.speaker: Jon Brodkin
insights.so_what: Politically connected capital is consolidating behind Polymarket, a competitive signal in the prediction-market duopoly.
insights.locator: Trump Jr. simultaneously has an interest in Polymarket

insights.claim: Trump Jr. received about $300,000 of Kalshi equity when he joined as strategic adviser in early 2025, when Kalshi was valued under $2 billion — less than a tenth of a later $22 billion valuation — and he may still hold a financial interest.
insights.speaker: Jon Brodkin
insights.so_what: Illustrates the stake's sharp mark-up and lingering political entanglement in Kalshi's cap table.
insights.locator: Trump Jr. may still have a financial interest

insights.claim: Kalshi CEO Tarek Mansour acknowledged an 'optics issue' with Trump Jr. and claimed the hire predated the election, but Kalshi actually named Trump Jr. a strategic advisor on January 13, 2025, more than two months after the November 2024 election, and Trump Jr. said he decided to help on Election Day.
insights.speaker: Jon Brodkin
insights.so_what: Management credibility on political ties is undermined by the timeline — a governance and reputational risk.
insights.quote: We are facing sort of an optics issue, I think.
insights.locator: Kalshi co-founder and CEO Tarek Mansour told MS Now

insights.claim: Mansour says Trump Jr. had no policy or regulatory involvement and was used as a marketing channel to his roughly 10 million followers to help Kalshi 'go direct,' which a spokesperson called a big part of its early online growth.
insights.speaker: Jon Brodkin
insights.so_what: Influencer-driven distribution was core to Kalshi's growth, raising dependence on high-profile personalities.
insights.quote: We never had any policy regulatory involvement
insights.locator: CEO claims no “regulatory involvement” for Trump Jr.

insights.claim: Kalshi was valued at $22 billion in a recent funding round and is reportedly in talks for a new round valuing it at $65 billion.
insights.speaker: Jon Brodkin
insights.so_what: Rapid valuation escalation signals strong investor appetite for prediction markets despite legal overhang.
insights.locator: Kalshi is reportedly in talks for a new funding round

insights.claim: Kalshi has paid former Democratic Senator Blanche Lincoln for lobbying since 2024; she helped write the 2010 law regulating prediction markets and once opposed event contracts for sports gambling, but now supports sports event contracts and opposes state regulation.
insights.speaker: Jon Brodkin
insights.so_what: Kalshi is building bipartisan lobbying cover, relevant to how durable its regulatory position is across administrations.
insights.locator: Kalshi has also paid former US Senator Blanche Lincoln

insights.claim: Senators Elizabeth Warren and Jeff Merkley warned White House Counsel Will Scharf that the Trump family is entangled with the prediction-market industry, citing a Trump teleprompter aide who made over $100,000 betting on Kalshi mention markets; the CFTC ordered Gabriel Perez to disgorge $107,539.02 and pay a $65,000 penalty.
insights.speaker: Jon Brodkin
insights.so_what: Insider-trading cases on mention markets are a live integrity and regulatory risk for prediction-market platforms.
insights.quote: should have been a wake-up call to the entire administration to enforce stronger ethics policies.
insights.locator: Trump family “entangled with the success of this industry”

insights.claim: Trump Media and Technology Group announced a 'Truth Predict' prediction market for Truth Social in partnership with Crypto.com but appears to have scaled back the plan.
insights.speaker: Jon Brodkin
insights.so_what: A potential politically connected entrant seems to be retreating, easing competitive pressure on Kalshi and Polymarket.
insights.locator: Trump Media and Technology Group last year announced plans

insights.claim: The Trump administration's CFTC has taken a permissive approach to prediction markets, filed briefs supporting Kalshi, and sued 11 states — most recently Arkansas — to block state regulation, while state attorneys general accuse Kalshi of illegal gambling.
insights.speaker: Jon Brodkin
insights.so_what: Federal preemption backing is the key pillar of prediction-market growth; a change in administration could remove it.
insights.locator: The Trump administration has helped prediction markets grow

insights.claim: The CFTC is reportedly close to charging Kalshi for failing to properly notify the agency about dozens of new event contracts, even as it fights states on Kalshi's behalf.
insights.speaker: Jon Brodkin
insights.so_what: Federal enforcement risk exists even under a friendly regulator — watch for charges ahead of Kalshi's funding round.
insights.locator: The CFTC reportedly is close to bringing charges

insights.claim: Kalshi has lost multiple cases in which appeals and district courts refused to block state gambling laws, and a Louisiana court issued a temporary restraining order against Kalshi, Polymarket, Coinbase, Robinhood and other operators, touted by Attorney General Liz Murrill.
insights.speaker: Jon Brodkin
insights.so_what: State-level injunctions threaten prediction-market revenue at brokers like Coinbase and Robinhood, not just Kalshi.
insights.quote: It’s not complicated: if you aren’t a licensed gaming operator, you aren’t legal,
insights.locator: Kalshi has lost a number of cases

insights.claim: Kalshi argues all its wagers, even those functionally identical to sports bets, are federally regulated event contracts (swaps); its biggest win came against New Jersey in the Third Circuit, which New Jersey is asking the Supreme Court to overturn, with the Trump administration expected to back Kalshi if the case is taken.
insights.speaker: Jon Brodkin
insights.so_what: A Supreme Court ruling would be the binary catalyst for the legality of sports event contracts nationwide.
insights.locator: Kalshi argues that all its wagers
